data.current_description: Use for what sells best in a department right now. The rank is Amazon's, not a sales figure. Best-seller rankings for a department of one marketplace, 50 per page. Every answer carries the department it resolved to and how (category_resolution: by slug, name or a fragment of a name, with a hint when a fragment such as 'shoes' landed on the whole 'Clothing, Shoes & Jewelry' department, or 'subcategory' when a word such as 'camera' named a subcategory), available_categories (that marketplace's departments with slugs; MCP: with compact=false) and available_subcategories (the children of the node shown, with the ids subcategory_code takes). On amazon.com subcategory_code also takes any browse node id at any depth, or a name resolved under the department ("women's shoes", "mules & clogs"); category.subcategory_path gives the node's full path and category.heading the page's own title line.
data.description_suggestion: Retrieve best-seller rankings for a marketplace category or department. Returns up to 50 ranked products per page with their position within the requested list. Accepts category as a slug, display name, or unique fragment; category_resolution indicates how the input was resolved (by slug, name, or fragment match) and provides hints when ambiguous. Response includes available_categories (all departments with slugs for that marketplace) and available_subcategories (child nodes of the selected category). On amazon.com, subcategory_code accepts any browse node ID at any depth or a name within the department. Each result row includes rank (position on the current page), product details, and category metadata (subcategory_path for full hierarchy, heading for page title). No required parameters—calling bare returns US appliances page 1. Page is capped at 5.
